title: Ezért: Linking the Problem to What You Do Next

sections.title: From problem to plan, in one breath
sections.content: You already know ezért ("that's why, therefore") from early on. It's the connector that turns a report into a real, flowing exchange: state the problem, then use ezért to move straight into what you're doing about it — a request, an appointment change, or the fact that it's solved. Real conversations rarely stop at just naming a problem; ezért is how you keep going.

sections.title: Problem, then ezért
rows: The air conditioning broke. That's why I'm complaining.
Nem működik a wifi. Ezért kérek egy másik szobát.
The wifi doesn't work. That's why I'm asking for a different room.
Beteg vagyok. Ezért szeretnék lemondani egy időpontot.
I'm sick. That's why I'd like to cancel an appointment.

items.spanish: Hiányzik egy törölköző, ezért szükségem van segítségre.
items.english: A towel is missing, that's why I need help.

items.spanish: Elromlott a telefonom, ezért szeretnék egy időpontot módosítani.
items.english: My phone broke, that's why I'd like to change an appointment.

sections.content: ezért can start a brand-new sentence or follow a comma inside the same one — both are natural, so pick whichever rhythm fits what you're saying.
